organization: HIV Education and Prevention Project of Alameda County (HEPPAC)
program: Harm reduction, overdose prevention, treatment navigation, drug checking, and wraparound services

nutshell.headline: HEPPAC addresses fatal overdose and infection risks, but current organization-level outcomes and the next-gift counterfactual are not public.
nutshell.body: Under an explicitly judgmental prior-weighted illustration, a $100,000 unrestricted gift corresponds to $10.86 million per better life (10 modeled QALYs), or $12.38 million under an illustrative gross-resource sensitivity. The central whole-organization accounting diagnostic is $6.73 million in reported spending per 10 scenario-attributed QALYs. Neither is an empirically identified marginal quote.
nutshell.whyItMayWork: Naloxone rescue, medication treatment, and sterile-syringe access have credible severe-endpoint mechanisms. HEPPAC operates an integrated East Bay harm-reduction portfolio and its official donation page says gifts support community services.
nutshell.whyWeAreCautious: HEPPAC does not publicly report current unique participants, annual reversals, retained medication treatment, infections averted, checking-linked behavior or cross-program overlap. A same-system navigation study is observational and noncurrent, and a newer randomized peer-navigation trial was inconclusive.
nutshell.recommendationBlocker: Obtain a dated next-$100,000 budget, successor-contract status, current unduplicated people and events, treatment starts and retention, infection outcomes, drug-checking behavior, residence shares, and person-level cross-program linkage before recommending a gift on health cost-effectiveness.

summary.label: MODELED ORDINARY GIFT
summary.detail: prior-weighted donor cost per 10 modeled QALYs; includes a 20% no-benefit prior

summary.label: CENTRAL GIFT ILLUSTRATION
summary.detail: per 10 modeled QALYs; 45% deployability and 85% realization are analyst priors

summary.label: WHOLE-ORG DIAGNOSTIC
summary.detail: reported annual spending per 10 central scenario QALYs; not marginal donor cost

summary.label: BAY / SF SHARE
summary.detail: QALY-weighted assumed shares; SF is nested within Bay and neither is measured residence

summary.label: FUNDING ROOM
summary.detail: moderate reserves, but no priced next-gift use and a public amendment only maintained existing staffing

programSection.body: HEPPAC is an Oakland nonprofit serving Alameda and Contra Costa Counties. Its portfolio includes overdose-prevention education and naloxone, syringe access, medication-treatment navigation, HIV/HCV services, drug checking, mobile outreach, drop-in basic needs, wound care, condoms, acupuncture/herbalist services, and B-DUHB interventions. Its donation page also identifies fiscal sponsorship for Punks With Lunch and J&MP Innovations.

steps.title: Prevent and reverse overdose
steps.detail: OPEND distributes naloxone with brief training. Refill access is unlimited, so doses, people and reversal events require separate deduplication.

steps.title: Link people to medication treatment
steps.detail: Substance-use navigators may improve 30-day engagement, but HEPPAC publishes no current annual starts, medication mix or retained treatment-years.

steps.title: Reduce infection and supply risk
steps.detail: Syringe access has credible HIV-prevention evidence; FTIR and confirmatory drug checking may change behavior, but HEPPAC-specific infections and overdoses averted are not measured publicly.

steps.title: Provide integrated support
steps.detail: Screening/linkage, mobile outreach, condoms, drop-in services, wound care, acupuncture/herbalist services and B-DUHB may add value. They remain in cost and receive no separate QALYs here.

programSection.boundary: The model uses the entire FY2025 expense of $4,953,186. Events, items and people are never summed as recipients. Naloxone, navigation and checking share mortality endpoints and receive an explicit overlap sensitivity; person-level overlap remains unresolved. Fiscal-sponsorship/pass-through activity inside expense is also unresolved.

model.headline: Prior-weighted modeled ordinary gift: $10.86M per 10 QALYs; central: $17.60M.
model.body: The executable first models annual organization-attributed QALYs under explicit pathway, causal-additionality and overlap judgments. It then scales a hypothetical $100,000 unrestricted gift pro rata to annual expense, applies funding deployability and realization discounts, and weights downside, central, favorable and no-benefit cases. The separate gross-resource figures are illustrative multipliers, not measured estimates or lower bounds.

equation.label: CENTRAL MODELED GIFT COST
equation.expression: 10 × $100,000 ÷ [7.357 central annual organization-attributed QALYs × ($100,000 ÷ $4,953,186 expense) × 45% deployability × 85% realization]

inputs.label: Annual retained-effective treatment engagements
inputs.basis: No current HEPPAC outcome volume exists. Anderson et al. observed 119 SUN recipients within a five-month, all-SUD, noncurrent cohort; it is transfer context and is never annualized into HEPPAC outcomes.

inputs.label: QALY per retained-effective engagement
inputs.basis: Sordo et al. supports the direction of benefit while in treatment, not these magnitudes. Drug mix, retained years, mortality risk difference, morbidity and local transfer are missing.

inputs.label: Annual reported reversal events
inputs.basis: Twenty and 50 are scenario values. The 137 figure is an old snapshot with no clean annual window and appears only in the favorable stress case.

inputs.label: Otherwise-fatal probability and HEPPAC attribution
inputs.basis: Lay naloxone survival is high, but the untreated counterfactual and alternative rescue are not observed.

inputs.label: Finite survival-adjusted QALYs per fatal event
inputs.basis: Discounted finite sums use 5/10/20-year horizons, annual survival 65%/75%/82%, utility 0.55/0.65/0.75 and 3% discounting.

inputs.label: Infections averted and QALYs
inputs.basis: Syringe-service evidence supports HIV prevention, but HEPPAC publishes no unique exposure, baseline incidence or local infections-averted analysis.

inputs.label: Fatal-overdose equivalents from drug checking
inputs.basis: Behavior evidence is emerging and mortality is not established. If the proposed 50 samples/month occurred, these imply one equivalent per 12,000/2,400/600 samples.

inputs.label: Shared mortality overlap adjustment
inputs.basis: Naloxone, navigation and checking may benefit the same person and share survival endpoints. This sensitivity does not solve deduplication.

inputs.label: Pathway outcome additionality
inputs.basis: Separates service activity from outcomes that would not otherwise occur; retained in both whole-organization and gift calculations.

inputs.label: Ordinary-gift funding/capacity deployability
inputs.basis: Moderate reserves and substantial contributions allow some marginal use, but HEPPAC has not made a dated next-$100,000 commitment and public funding may be displaced.

inputs.label: Gift-to-outcome realization
inputs.basis: Discounts implementation delay and failure between receipt, service expansion and health outcome.

inputs.label: Unconditional scenario prior weights
inputs.basis: A material null reflects missing current outcomes and inconclusive navigation evidence. The favorable case is low-weight because it combines several unobserved favorable assumptions.

inputs.label: Illustrative gross-resource multiplier
inputs.basis: Flags free state naloxone, partners and clinical referrals without claiming quantities, fair values or a lower bound.

inputs.label: Bay Area impact share
inputs.basis: Documented program sites are in Alameda and Contra Costa Counties; beneficiary residence is not measured.

inputs.label: San Francisco impact share, nested in Bay
inputs.basis: No SF site was found, but that does not exclude SF residents. Zero applies only to the downside assumption, not as a measured fact.

sensitivity.headline: No positive QALYs
sensitivity.detail: The gift and an assumed 1.10× gross resource amount are spent; QALYs are zero and stand-alone cost is infinite.

sensitivity.headline: $1.242M modeled donor cost per 10 QALYs
sensitivity.detail: 0.80542 gift QALY; $1.614M illustrative gross-resource sensitivity; this case still supplies most weighted QALYs.

sensitivity.headline: $10.86M modeled donor cost per 10 QALYs
sensitivity.detail: 0.092049 expected gift QALY; $12.38M illustrative gross-resource sensitivity; 97.76% Bay and 4.09% nested SF outcome shares are assumed, not measured.

model.uncertaintyBoundary: Scenario values and weights are analyst priors, not confidence intervals, observed HEPPAC outcomes or empirically calibrated probabilities. The favorable stress case contributes most expected QALYs despite only 8% weight, so the headline is right-tail-sensitive. Zero deployability or zero outcomes returns zero QALYs and no finite cost ratio. The five-month Anderson study is never annualized.
model.fundingBoundary: RFMF is plausible but unverified. FY2025 net assets of $2.363M equal about 5.7 months of expense and the organization ran a $209K surplus. The November 14, 2025 county staff recommendation requested a $700K increase through August 31, 2026 primarily to maintain existing navigator staffing; without an executed amendment or later budget, it is a dated public-funding baseline rather than a verified gap. HEPPAC's donation page gives examples and says donations support services, but it does not price health-outcome capacity or commit the next $100,000. Verified marginal donor and gross costs remain unknown.

evidence.design: Observational implementation study with propensity matching
evidence.population: 1,328 discharged patients with alcohol, opioid, cocaine or methamphetamine diagnoses at three Alameda public emergency departments, September 1, 2021–January 31, 2022
evidence.result: 119 received navigation; 30-day treatment engagement was 50.4% versus 15.9%; matched OR 2.1 (95% CI 1.2–3.5).
evidence.transfer: Same-system mechanism evidence only. It is a five-month, noncurrent, all-SUD study and supplies no annual HEPPAC outcome volume, retained MOUD or mortality.

evidence.population: 247 NYC emergency-department patients after opioid overdose
evidence.result: Composite adverse-event RR 1.02 (0.72–1.45); mortality HR 0.55 (0.22–1.30); 90-day MOUD OR 1.64 (0.68–3.94).
evidence.transfer: Inconclusive rather than proof of no effect; mortality was underpowered and the peer model differs from Alameda medication-first navigation. It prevents treating observational linkage as certain mortality benefit.

evidence.result: Reported survival after lay naloxone was 93–98% across uncontrolled studies.
evidence.transfer: Supports rescue efficacy but does not reveal which HEPPAC reversals would otherwise be fatal or rescued elsewhere.

evidence.population: People who inject drugs using syringe-service programs
evidence.result: Evidence was sufficient for HIV prevention; higher-quality studies in one meta-analysis reported RR 0.42 (0.22–0.81).
evidence.transfer: Local incidence, coverage, unique users and overlap with other providers are absent, so the model varies infections averted directly.

evidence.result: Evidence suggests changes in intentions and sometimes behavior; mortality effects are not established.
evidence.transfer: HEPPAC drug-checking receives small central credit and a clearly labeled favorable stress assumption.

evidence.result: FY2025 revenue $5.162M, expense $4.953M, surplus $209K and net assets $2.363M.
evidence.transfer: Full expense is the whole-organization denominator; fiscal-sponsorship/pass-through composition and marginal funding remain unresolved.

reservations: Current unique participants, kits or doses, reversal events, treatment starts and retention, checking-linked behavior, infections and cross-program linkage are not publicly reported.
Unlimited naloxone refills make item, person and event deduplication essential; reported reversals are not deaths averted.
Navigation, naloxone and checking may benefit the same person and share mortality; an overlap sensitivity is not person-level deduplication.
MOUD QALYs per retained-effective engagement are bounded sensitivities, not estimates derived quantitatively from the Sordo meta-analysis.
Fatal-event QALYs use finite survival, utility and discounting priors; age, relapse, competing mortality and event timing are unobserved.
Gift deployability, realization, scenario weights, geography and gross multipliers are analyst priors.
The $700K county document is a staff-requested amendment to maintain staffing, not evidence in this packet of execution, expiry-created need or private-gift additionality.
Bay and SF shares are service-geography-informed assumptions; beneficiary residence is unknown.
The gross-resource multiplier is illustrative only, neither measured nor a demonstrated lower bound.
Fiscal sponsorship/pass-through activity may be included in expense, but this packet cannot reconcile it.
excludedBenefits: Drop-in showers, laundry, food, hygiene supplies and resource navigation
HIV/HCV screening, counseling, referral and treatment linkage distinct from syringe prevention
Community and mobile outreach, condoms, education, advocacy and task-force effects
Abscess wound care and other community-based medical services
Benefits attributable to fiscally sponsored or pass-through programs not reconciled to HEPPAC expense
Criminal-justice, housing, dignity, stigma and emergency-service outcomes
